entries.label: CPTS arsenal
entries.detail: Command-first pentest reference along the Cyber Kill Chain: search by port, service or tool

entries.label: CPTS: Reconnaissance
entries.detail: Map the target: hosts, open ports, services, versions, and the people and names around them. Passive OSINT first, then active scanning and enumeration.

entries.label: CPTS: Weaponisation
entries.detail: Turn a finding into something that will run on the target: a payload, a crafted document, a wordlist tuned to the environment.

entries.label: CPTS: Delivery
entries.detail: Get the payload or request to the target: a web request, an upload, a phishing email, a captured protocol.

entries.label: CPTS: Exploitation
entries.detail: Trigger the flaw and get first execution or access: a service exploit, a web vulnerability, a weak credential.

entries.label: CPTS: Installation
entries.detail: Make access durable and usable: a shell upgrade, a foothold, local privilege escalation, persistence.

entries.label: CPTS: Command & Control
entries.detail: Operate the foothold: a stable channel back to the operator, tasking, and tunnelling to reach deeper.

entries.label: CPTS: Actions on Objectives
entries.detail: Achieve the engagement goal: credential access, lateral movement, domain and data objectives, and the evidence for the report.

entries.label: ffuf — Web fuzzing
entries.detail: A fast web fuzzer that puts the FUZZ keyword anywhere in a request: paths, parameters, headers, POST bodies and Host for vhosts. The flexible companion to Gobuster when you need recursion, filtering or to fuzz something other than a path.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: Gobuster — Web content discovery
entries.detail: Brute-forces hidden web content: directories and files, DNS subdomains, and virtual hosts. Run it against any HTTP or HTTPS service once a port scan finds one.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: NetExec — Network and AD enumeration
entries.detail: The successor to CrackMapExec. Sweeps a subnet for SMB, WinRM, LDAP, MSSQL and more, checks credentials across hosts, lists shares and users, and flags where a credential is a local admin. The workhorse of internal and Active Directory enumeration.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: Nmap — Network scanning
entries.detail: The port scanner. Finds live hosts, open ports, service versions and, through NSE scripts, a first pass of service enumeration. Usually the first command run against an in-scope network.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: msfvenom — Payload generation
entries.detail: The Metasploit payload generator. Produces reverse and bind shells in the format the target can run — exe, elf, war, aspx, raw shellcode — ready to pair with a listener. The standard way to make a payload for an authorised test.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: Responder — LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning
entries.detail: Answers LLMNR, NBT-NS and mDNS name-resolution requests on the local segment, so a host looking for a mistyped or missing name connects to you instead and hands over an NTLMv2 hash. A top source of first credentials on an internal test.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: Hydra — Credential attacks
entries.detail: Online password guessing against a live service: SSH, FTP, RDP, web login forms and many more. Use it for a targeted spray with a short, sensible list, not a blind dictionary run.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: Metasploit Framework — Exploitation framework
entries.detail: The exploitation framework: a searchable library of exploits and payloads, the multi/handler that catches shells, Meterpreter for post-exploitation, and routing for pivoting. The hub that ties weaponisation, exploitation and C2 together.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: sqlmap — SQL injection
entries.detail: Automates finding and exploiting SQL injection. Confirms the flaw, fingerprints the database, dumps data, and — where the configuration allows — reads files or gets command execution. Point it at a request you suspect is injectable.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: PEASS-ng (linPEAS / winPEAS) — Privilege escalation enumeration
entries.detail: The privilege-escalation scouts. linPEAS and winPEAS enumerate a host for local privesc routes — weak permissions, stored credentials, misconfigured services, sudo and SUID, scheduled tasks — and colour-code the most promising findings. Run one the moment you land a shell.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: Chisel — Tunnelling and pivoting
entries.detail: A fast TCP/UDP tunnel over HTTP, in a single Go binary for every platform. Builds a SOCKS proxy or port-forward through a compromised host so your tools on the outside can reach an internal network you otherwise cannot touch.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: BloodHound — Active Directory attack paths
entries.detail: Maps Active Directory as a graph and finds the shortest path from where you are to Domain Admin. A collector (SharpHound or the Python collector) gathers users, groups, sessions, ACLs and trusts; BloodHound shows who can reach what, and how.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: Evil-WinRM — Remote access (WinRM)
entries.detail: A clean interactive shell over WinRM (Windows Remote Management). Give it a password or an NTLM hash and, if the account is in Remote Management Users, you get a PowerShell session with handy upload, download and in-memory script loading built in.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes

entries.label: Impacket — Windows and AD protocol tooling
entries.detail: A toolbox of Python scripts that speak Windows protocols directly. secretsdump pulls hashes, the exec scripts (psexec, wmiexec) give remote shells, and GetUserSPNs/GetNPUsers pull Kerberos tickets to crack. The backbone of Active Directory attacks from Linux.
entries.words: When to reach for it Key flags Commands Workflow Notes
